name: application-modals
title: Modals
description: Dialog panels that overlay the page to capture focused attention for confirmations, forms, and critical actions.
useWhen: Requesting explicit user confirmation before a destructive or irreversible action.
Collecting a small amount of input (e.g., a name, email, or quick setting) without leaving the current page.
Displaying additional detail or a secondary action flow without a full page navigation.
avoidWhen: The content requires significant scrolling — use a dedicated page or slide-over panel instead.
The action is not urgent and can be deferred — do not interrupt user flow unnecessarily.
The modal would open another modal — nested dialogs are inaccessible and disorienting.
responsiveBehavior: Modals are centered on desktop and expand to near-full-screen on mobile viewports. Maximum width should be constrained so content remains readable on wide screens.
accessibility: Use the native <dialog> element or role="dialog" with aria-modal="true" to trap focus and announce the dialog.
On open, move focus to the first interactive element or the dialog title.
Escape key must close the dialog and return focus to the element that triggered it.
The page behind the modal must be inert — use the inert attribute or a focus trap.

variants.title: Base
variants.description: Plain dialog panel with a title and body text — the minimal pattern for informational confirmations.
accessibility: Focus moves to the dialog on open; Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.

variants.title: Base (Dark)
variants.description: Plain informational dialog adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Dark dialog background and text colors must meet WCAG AA contrast requirements.

variants.title: Base with close
variants.description: Informational dialog with an X close button in the top-right corner for explicit dismissal.
accessibility: Close button must have an aria-label='Close dialog'; Escape should also close the dialog.

variants.title: Base with close (Dark)
variants.description: Informational dialog with close button adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Close button icon and hover state must remain visible against dark dialog backgrounds.

variants.title: Actions
variants.description: Dialog with a primary action and cancel button in the footer — for confirmations and simple decision prompts.
accessibility: Initial focus should land on the less destructive action (Cancel) in confirmation dialogs.

variants.title: Actions (Dark)
variants.description: Confirm/cancel action dialog adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Button colors must maintain contrast for both primary and cancel states on dark backgrounds.

variants.title: Actions with close
variants.description: Confirm/cancel action dialog that also includes a corner X close button for explicit dismissal.
accessibility: Three close paths (Escape, X button, Cancel) give users multiple keyboard-accessible ways to dismiss.

variants.title: Actions with close (Dark)
variants.description: Action dialog with corner close button adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: All three close paths must be keyboard-operable; button colors must meet contrast on dark backgrounds.

variants.title: Input
variants.description: Dialog containing a form input field for collecting a single piece of information such as a name or URL.
accessibility: Focus moves directly to the input on dialog open; input must have a visible linked label.

variants.title: Input (Dark)
variants.description: Single-input dialog adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Input border, label, and placeholder colors must meet contrast requirements on dark backgrounds.

variants.title: Input with close
variants.description: Single-input dialog with an X close button, combining input collection with an explicit dismiss affordance.
accessibility: Focus moves to the input; close button has aria-label='Close dialog'; Escape also dismisses.

variants.title: Input with close (Dark)
variants.description: Single-input dialog with close button adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Input, close button, and footer action colors must meet WCAG AA on dark backgrounds.
